report:
Fresh complete followup review of content.blocks. Saved/read the prior report and inputs, started fresh, recaptured the source helper, and compared every fragment. Claim, complete test and helper are unchanged. The sole spec.rs change is an implementation_references association comment before its unknown-name validator; no parser or finish_anchor code changed.

The full claim requires content after the definition marker to include every subsequent Markdown block until the first applicable closing boundary, with blank lines preserving paragraphs, lists, tables and code in one claim. The sole ordinary associated implementation finish_anchor slices original source from marker end through the supplied boundary, trims only exterior whitespace, records matching source offsets and consumes the active anchor. It does not reconstruct selected Markdown events, so interior formatting and blocks remain intact. The surrounding captured parser sets the start at the definition-name token end; paragraph ends clear only paragraph tracking and code events only change literal context. Blank lines and ordinary block transitions do not finalize content. New valid definitions, actual headings, explicit ends and source end close content in source order, while literal/HTML handling prevents false boundaries. The marker-only delta cannot affect these operations.

The complete sole ordinary test claims_retain_all_blocks_until_the_next_definition_or_document_end supplies Unicode prose, a separate qualifying paragraph, multiple list items, a table, fenced Unicode Rust code, indented code and a blockquote, separated by blank lines. It requires no diagnostics and exact first.content equality with the entire body. It then requires the second anchor's same-line Unicode prose and later paragraph to equal the exact trimmed expected text. Both content spans must slice the original source into their stored content, and the first extent must end before the next marker. These assertions directly verify listed block types, blank-line continuity, marker exclusion, nonoverlap and next-definition/source-end closure. Other particular boundary permutations have dedicated claims; this assessment does not claim their exhaustive tests were run here. The recaptured source helper simply wraps the input in SpecSource and leaves assertions visible in the test.

No TODO/N/A entries or deferred aspects exist for this block-retention claim. Comparing the actual single-comment delta with the prior complete assessment confirms all requirements remain supported by current source and substantive assertions. No source changes, build or behavioral tests were performed; only fresh review commands and source inspection. No requested edits.
